reason: Recurrent Grade 3-4 toxicities in an older adult signal high risk of functional decline despite preserved ECOG 1. Geriatric assessment emphasizes that cumulative toxicity often precedes decompensation, and short-term mortality risk is underestimated without considering frailty and comorbidity burden.
evidences: Geriatric assessment emphasizes cumulative toxicity and frailty risk
ECOG 1 may underestimate vulnerability in older adults with multi-organ toxicities
